In [[differential geometry]], '''Yau's conjecture''' is a [[mathematical conjecture]] which states that any closed [[Riemannian manifold|Riemannian]] [[3-manifold]] contains infinitely many [[Differentiable_manifold#Definition|smooth]] [[Closed manifold|closed]] [[Immersion (mathematics)#Immersed plane curves|immersed]] [[minimal surface]]s. It is named after [[Shing-Tung Yau]], who posed it as the 88th entry in his 1982 list of open problems in differential geometry.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last1=Yau|first1=Shing Tung|zbl=0479.53001|title=Problem section|encyclopedia=Seminar on Differential Geometry|pages=669–706|series=Annals of Mathematics Studies|volume=102|publisher=[[Princeton University Press]]|location=Princeton, NJ|year=1982|editor-last1=Yau|editor-first1=Shing-Tung|doi=10.1515/9781400881918-035|isbn=978-1-4008-8191-8|mr=0645762|author-link1=Shing-Tung Yau}}</ref>

The conjecture was first resolved by [[Fernando Codá Marques]] and [[André Neves]] in the case of positive [[Ricci curvature]]. Then, for the case of [[Generic property|generic]] metrics, there are independent solutions from Kei Irie, [[Fernando Codá Marques]] and [[André Neves]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Irie |first1=Kei |last2=Marques |first2=Fernando C. |author-link2=Fernando Codá Marques |last3=Neves |first3=André |author-link3=André Neves |year=2018|title=Density of minimal hypersurfaces for generic metrics |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=187|issue=3|pages=963–972|doi=10.4007/annals.2018.187.3.8|doi-access=free|arxiv=1710.10752 }}</ref>, Otis Chodosh and Christos Mantoulidis<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chodosh |first=Otis |last2=Mantoulidis |first2=Christos |date=2020-01-01 |title=Minimal surfaces and the Allen--Cahn equation on 3-manifolds: index, multiplicity, and curvature estimates |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematics/volume-191/issue-1/Minimal-surfaces-and-the-Allen--Cahn-equation-on-3/10.4007/annals.2020.191.1.4.full |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=191 |issue=1 |doi=10.4007/annals.2020.191.1.4 |issn=0003-486X|arxiv=1803.02716 }}</ref>, and also Xin Zhou<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhou |first=Xin |date=2020-11-01 |title=On the Multiplicity One Conjecture in min-max theory |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematics/volume-192/issue-3/On-the-Multiplicity-One-Conjecture-in-min-max-theory/10.4007/annals.2020.192.3.3.full |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=192 |issue=3 |doi=10.4007/annals.2020.192.3.3 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>. Finally, [[Antoine Song]] proved the conjectures for all metrics.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Song |first1=Antoine |author-link1=Antoine Song|title=Existence of infinitely many minimal hypersurfaces in closed manifolds |year=2023|pages=859–895|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=197|issue=3|doi=10.4007/annals.2023.197.3.1|doi-access=free|arxiv=1806.08816}}</ref> The proofs above use [[Almgren–Pitts min-max theory|min-max theory]], which is a form of infinite dimensional [[Morse theory]] for the area functional. A proof for the generic metric case via gluing construction was also later found by Adrian Chun-Pong Chu and Daniel Stern<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chu |first=Adrian Chun-Pong |last2=Stern |first2=Daniel |date=2025-09-23 |title=Minimal surface doublings and electrostatics for Schr\"odinger operators |url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18630v1 |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=arXiv.org |language=en}}</ref>, in which the minimal surfaces constructed have bounded area but unbounded genus.
